summary: The main article describes a dual gold/photoredox-catalyzed C(sp)-H arylation of terminal alkynes. It includes one table for reaction optimization and five schemes detailing the reaction scope, mechanistic proposals, and further synthetic applications of the products.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Gold-catalyzed C -C and C -X bond-forming coupling reactions proposed to proceed via Au I /Au III redox cycles.
items.description: Illustrates various gold-catalyzed oxidative heterofunctionalization and C-H functionalization strategies, including the dual gold/photoredox approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reaction optimization a
items.description: Lists the screening of gold catalysts, photocatalysts, and light sources to optimize the yield of the cross-coupled product 3aa.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Dual Au/photoredox-catalyzed arylation of di ff erent alkynes.
items.description: Shows the substrate scope for various alkyl and aromatic terminal alkynes using a specific aryldiazonium salt.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Dual Au/photoredox-catalyzed arylation of 1f and 1c with substituted benzenediazonium salts.
items.description: Explores the electronic and steric scope of various aryldiazonium salts in the coupling reaction with two different alkynes.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Further manipulation of cross-coupled products (see the ESI † for experimental details).
items.description: Demonstrates the utility of the synthesized arylalkynes in subsequent palladium-catalyzed Sonogashira and Suzuki coupling reactions.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Mechanistic proposal.
items.description: Proposes a catalytic cycle involving photoredox-induced SET, aryl radical addition to Au(I), and subsequent reductive elimination from a Au(III) intermediate.
